subject: Helix reference architecture runway: technical review & launch checklist
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helix Solutions - ENG <eng+helix@helixsolutions.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Helix reference architecture runway: technical review & launch checklist

Hi Morgan / Helix eng team,

Thanks again for taking the time to partner on the reference deployment for your Gateway product. Attached is the first-pass reference architecture (helix-reference-arch-v1.pdf) and a proposed staging test plan (helix-staging-test-plan.xlsx).

High-level asks from Redwood before we sign off for a joint launch lab:
- Confirm the model serving topology you expect to exercise (single-model vs multi-model fanout)
- Expected peak qps and 95th percentile latency SLO targets for the proof-of-concept
- Any custom operator/third-party kernel usage that would affect runtime selection
- Which data flows need KV/prefix caching (customer prompt prefixes, session affinity)

We'd like to run a 2-day smoke + load window in our staging next week (May 26-27) to verify: model load times, KV cache warming, batching behavior, and failover to a lower-cost variant. Sergio will coordinate the runbook.

CCing Sergio and Marissa from Partnerships to capture ops/runbook items and launch comms. Can you confirm tech owners and a preferred time window?

Thanks,
Priyom
Principal Partner Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix-reference-arch-v1.pdf (diagram), helix-staging-test-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Helix Solutions - ENG <eng+helix@helixsolutions.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Morgan Patel <morgan@stoneridge.consulting>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix reference architecture runway: technical review & launch checklist

Hi Priyom / team,

Thanks — reviewed the PDF and spreadsheet with our SRE/eng leads. Quick notes and open questions: 

1) Topology: our Gateway normally runs a fanout for embeddings + reranking, but for the joint reference we propose a single inference model endpoint with optional sidecar reranking to keep latencies deterministic. That maps well to Redwood's serving runtime.

2) Performance targets: for the joint example let's aim for 2k sustained qps with a 95th <= 180ms for the generate path (we'll validate with a 50k token/day representative dataset). Is that in-line with Redwood Dedicated profiles?

3) Third-party kernels: we use an optimized matmul kernel in our internal pipeline for long-context models. We'll share the build artifact list; it may require the runtime to select a specific kernel path.

4) Caching: we have two prefixes — session prompts (short-lived) and account templates (long-lived). We'll provide TTLs. Are you able to configure separate KV caches per tenant in Private/Dedicated?

5) Test-plan tweaks: added a column for "failure-injection" cases and a minimal acceptance criterion per test.

We're available to run the smoke window on May 26 in the afternoon PT. I'll add our SRE (morgan@stoneridge.consulting) as the on-call for the run.

—Eng (Helix)
Helix Solutions Engineering

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helix Solutions - ENG <eng+helix@helixsolutions.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix reference architecture runway: technical review & launch checklist

Thanks for the quick turnaround — this looks good. A few operational clarifications from the Redwood runbook POV:

- Throughput targets: Redwood Dedicated has instance profiles that comfortably cover a 2k sustained qps target; we'll use a small pool of g5x-like instances and tune batching. Can you confirm the average token-per-request distribution? That will drive our batching window.

- Kernel compatibility: if Helix needs the custom matmul kernel, we'll stage the kernel in a container layer and exercise it in an isolated run first. We'll need the build artifact and a checksum.

- KV cache per-tenant: yes, Dedicated and Private support namespace-level caches. For the reference deployment we'll wire two namespaces (session, templates) with the TTLs you provide. We'll add a cache-warm step to the smoke plan.

- Failure-injection: good call. We'll add an automated step to drop 10% of node heartbeats for 30s and verify fallback to compatible model variant. Please confirm acceptable blast radius.

Action items:
1) Helix: provide kernel artifact + checksums, TTL values for prefixes, and confirmation of token distribution (by Wed EOD).
2) Redwood (Sergio): publish runbook (redwood-smoke-runbook.md) and coordinate access for Helix SRE.
3) All: finalize test windows for May 26 (staging) — target start 14:00 PT.

I'll open a calendar event once we have confirmations.

—Sergio
Sr. Solutions Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Looping back — thanks everyone for the alignment. Confirming next steps and owners: 

- Helix (Morgan): provide kernel artifact + checksum, token distribution sample, TTLs for session/templates — due Wed 2027-05-26 09:00 PT.
- Redwood (Sergio): share redwood-smoke-runbook.md and calendar invite for May 26 14:00 PT.
- Priyom / Marissa: we'll prepare the joint tech note and a short press-facing blurb for partner comms after a successful run.

I'll circulate the calendar invite and a DocuSign link for the partner MOU once the kernel artifact is confirmed. If we hit the acceptance criteria during the smoke window, we'll schedule a joint customer-facing demo the week after.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Partnerships Lead
Redwood Inference
